takeaway: A robot stays up while its balance point is over the patch between its feet; four feet make a big patch, two make a tiny one.

selfCheck.question: Why does a humanoid take a small step when pushed?
selfCheck.answer: small patch; push moves the spot outside; stepping puts a foot down where the weight is going, moving the patch back under the balance point.

sentence: A robot stays standing as long as the spot on the floor directly below its balance point is inside the patch its feet cover. A four-legged robot has a big patch, so a push rarely moves that spot outside it. A two-legged robot has a small patch, so a push easily moves the spot outside and the robot has to step to catch itself. Walking is harder still, because fewer feet are on the ground at any moment.
